data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Safety-critical systems are designed under unified governance, so diversity can be mandated; decentralized operators may lack any authority to coordinate diversity.","A large service has a single failure surface under unified control, whereas a decentralized network's failure surface is distributed across independent decision-makers, complicating any diversity policy.","In safety-critical engineering, common-cause analysis is often grounded in detailed component-level models; for decentralized networks, the relevant dependencies may be opaque or proprietary."],"overturn_conditions":["Empirical failure data showing that decentralized nodes with heterogeneous dependencies fail independently even when the most common dependency is stressed.","Evidence that the large service's internal redundancy is not actually diverse, so it provides no protection beyond component count.","A theoretical result proving that, under the observed dependency distribution, the decentralized network's effective correlation is below the large service's for all relevant failure modes."],"shared_structure":["Multiple nominally independent units whose failure probability is dominated by a shared dependency.","Redundancy count does not reduce correlated risk if the units are identical with respect to the common cause.","Distinguishing true independence requires causal intervention on the shared dependency, not just observing low correlation under benign conditions."],"source_memory_refs":["Common-cause failure analysis in safety-critical systems: N redundant channels only reduce risk if their failure modes are diverse; repeated identical channels create a single shared cause that defeats the redundancy."],"transfer_claims":["Redundancy that is not diverse is vulnerable to common-cause failure, regardless of whether the units are operated independently.","Observed low correlation under normal conditions is insufficient to establish causal independence; active perturbation of suspected shared dependencies is required.","Network decentralization does not automatically produce diversity; without deliberate heterogeneity, it can converge on a hidden monoculture."]},"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services can exhibit lower correlated-failure resilience than a single large service with strictly more total internal redundancy, when the network's nodes share a hidden supply-chain monoculture (e.g., a common library or cloud provider). The network appears distributed, but a single latent defect propagates across the nodes, producing correlated failures that only manifest once a shared trigger activates the defect. The large service's internal redundancy, by contrast, can be deliberately diversified across different implementations and datacenters, suppressing correlation even if total component count is similar.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If operators in the decentralized network independently choose heterogeneous dependencies, so that no single dependency covers more than a small fraction of nodes, the shared-cause path is broken.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service's internal redundancy is implemented with identical components in the same location or configuration, it has no diversity advantage and may retain correlated failure risk.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If failures of the decentralized nodes remain uncorrelated under active stress of the suspected shared dependency, the hidden-monoculture mechanism is not operating here.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service cannot enforce internal diversity (e.g., regulatory or vendor lock-in), its redundancy does not guarantee reduced correlation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shared dependencies act as common-cause latent paths: each independent operator chooses the same commodity library or cloud substrate because it is cheapest or standard, so a latent bug or outage in that dependency becomes a single shared cause. The large service can internally mandate heterogeneous implementations (e.g., multiple independent storage engines, geographic and vendor diversity), converting would-be common causes into independent ones. Evidence that distinguishes truly independent failures from merely uncorrelated-until-shared-cause is: observing that node failures remain uncorrelated under controlled perturbation of the suspected shared dependency, or finding no statistically detectable joint tail dependence across nodes when that dependency is stressed. If stressing the shared dependency causes synchronized failures, the failures were not truly independent; they were conditionally independent given the dependency's normal state.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
